tickets.subject: Generation stalls at ~60% with Anthropic provider

messages.body: Running QBORT 0.1.0 on macOS 15.3, targeting 200 tickets against Claude via Anthropic. The run gets to roughly 120 tickets and the progress bar just freezes — no error dialog, but the last batch never resolves. Console shows "fetch failed: ETIMEDOUT" a couple times. I've retried twice with the same stall point. Any way to make batches retry automatically, or is my key rate-limited?

Thanks for the detail, Marcus. The ETIMEDOUT points at a transient network/rate-limit issue mid-batch rather than a bad key. In 0.1.0 a stalled batch won't auto-retry, so the run parks. Lower the concurrency in settings (try 2 batches) and reduce batch size — that usually clears the rate ceiling. We're tracking automatic per-batch retry for the next release.

tickets.subject: "App is damaged and can't be opened" on first launch

messages.body: Just downloaded the QBORT 0.1.0 zip from the GitHub release and macOS 15.2 throws "QBORT is damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Trash." I know it's unsigned, but the usual right-click > Open trick isn't even offered. What's the correct way to get past Gatekeeper here?

That message is Gatekeeper quarantining the unsigned build after download. Run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/QBORT.app` in Terminal (adjust the path to wherever you moved it), then launch normally. The right-click > Open path is suppressed once the "damaged" flag is set, which is why you didn't see it. That should clear it — let us know if it persists.

We love the JSON output, but our helpdesk import tooling only ingests CSV. Right now I'm writing a little script to flatten tickets.json into rows, but a native CSV export (one row per message, or per ticket with a messages column) would save the whole team a step. Is that on the roadmap?

Appreciate the request, Tomás — CSV export has come up a few times and it's a natural fit next to the JSON exporter. Quick question so we scope it right: would you prefer one row per ticket (with messages serialized into a column) or one row per message with a shared ticket id? Your flattening script suggests the latter.
One row per message with a ticket id is exactly what we'd want — that maps cleanly onto our importer. Thanks for considering it.

tickets.subject: Exported JSON malformed after large Ollama run

messages.body: On QBORT 0.1.0 (macOS 14.7) I ran 500 tickets through a local Ollama llama3.1 model. The run reported success, but when I open the exported tickets.json my parser chokes with "Unexpected end of JSON input". Looks truncated near the end. Smaller runs (50) export fine. Is the file getting written before generation finishes?

Thanks Hannah — truncation on the large run but not the small one is a useful clue. QBORT writes tickets.json atomically (temp file + rename), so a partial file usually means the write was interrupted rather than a normal flush. Can you confirm whether the app was still showing an active run when you opened the file, or had it fully returned to the idle state?
It had returned to idle and showed "500 tickets" in the panel. I opened the file a few seconds later. The app didn't crash.

Got it. If the panel counted 500 and it still truncated, that points at the coalesced write for the final batch dropping content rather than a mid-run interruption. Could you check the file size and whether it ends inside a ticket object (mid-string) versus at a clean array boundary? That tells us if it's a serialization cutoff vs. an encoding issue.
File is ~1.8 MB and it ends mid-string inside a "body" field — no closing braces or brackets. Definitely a cutoff, not clean.

That's what we needed. A mid-string cutoff on the final coalesced write is reproducible on our side at high ticket counts with local models that stream slowly. I'm filing this as a bug — the fix is to fully buffer the last batch before the atomic rename. As a workaround, splitting the run into two 250-ticket passes and merging avoids the truncation entirely.
Confirmed — two 250 passes both exported valid JSON. Thanks for digging in, I'll use that until the fix ships.

tickets.subject: How does the staff-response distribution actually work?

messages.body: The docs mention a target for staff responses per ticket but I can't find where it explains the distribution. If I set responses on, do all tickets get the same number of replies, or is it spread somehow? Trying to model a realistic mix for a demo dataset and want to understand what QBORT is doing under the hood before I tune it.

Good question, Devin — it's a spread, not a flat count. QBORT distributes replies around your target so some tickets get zero and others get several, approximating a real inbox rather than a uniform thread length. Setting the target to, say, 2 gives you a realistic mix centered near two replies. We'll get this written up more clearly in the docs since it's not obvious today.

tickets.subject: Generation stalls at ~60% with Anthropic provider

messages.body: Running QBORT 0.1.0 on macOS 15.3, generating 200 tickets against Claude via the Anthropic provider. Around batch 6 of 10 the progress bar freezes and never advances. Console shows "fetch failed: ETIMEDOUT" once, then nothing. The partial tickets.json does get written but stops at 118 tickets. Test connection passes fine before I start. Any way to make batches resume instead of hanging the whole run?

Thanks for the detail, Priya. That ETIMEDOUT is the Anthropic call for one batch dropping and the orchestrator waiting on it. Can you tell me your batch size (Settings > Batching) and whether it reproduces at a smaller count like 40? I'd like to see if it's concurrency-related.
Batch size is 20, concurrency 4. At 40 tickets it finished clean twice in a row, no stall. It only wedges on the bigger runs.

That lines up with what we're seeing: a single timed-out batch currently blocks the pool instead of failing fast and retrying. Fix is landing in 0.1.1 to bound each batch with a timeout and re-queue it. As a workaround, drop concurrency to 2 for the 200-count run. I'll follow up here when the build is out.

tickets.subject: Exported tickets.json has malformed entries (trailing commas / cut off)

messages.body: After a 150-ticket Ollama run using llama3.1:8b, the exported tickets.json won't parse — my loader throws "Unexpected token } in JSON" near the end. Opening it, the last ticket object looks truncated and there's a dangling comma. QBORT 0.1.0, macOS 14.6. Did the write get interrupted, or is the export not atomic?

Sorry you hit that, Sofia. Writes are supposed to be atomic and coalesced, so a truncated file usually means the run errored mid-flight and the last partial batch got flushed. Was there anything in the app log around the end of the run — an Ollama disconnect or an out-of-memory from the model?
Now that I check the log, yes — "ollama: connection reset" right before it stopped. The Ollama server probably got OOM-killed on that machine.

That explains it. When the provider connection drops mid-batch we currently still write what assembled, which can leave a partial tail. The file should still be valid JSON though — a dangling comma is a real bug on our side, so I'm filing it. In the meantime, a smaller model or fewer concurrent batches will keep Ollama from getting killed.
Filed as a bug and linked to your ticket. Fix will ensure the on-disk file is always well-formed even when a run aborts partway. Thanks for the log line — that pinned it down fast.

We love using QBORT to seed our Zendesk sandbox, but the importer there wants CSV, not JSON. Right now I'm running a little jq script to convert every export, which is fine but flattening the nested responses is annoying. Could you add a native CSV export (one row per ticket, and ideally an option for one row per message)? Would save the whole team a step.

Good request, Devon — CSV export is something we've heard before. Quick question so I can scope it right: for the message-per-row option, would you want the ticket-level fields (subject, status, customer) repeated on each message row, or a separate tickets file plus a messages file keyed by ticket id?
Repeated on each row would be ideal — single flat file is easiest for the Zendesk importer to map. Thanks for considering it.

tickets.subject: How is the staff-response distribution actually decided?

messages.body: The docs mention a target number of staff responses per ticket, but I can't tell if that's an average across the run, a per-ticket exact count, or something weighted. I need my synthetic data to have a realistic spread of thread lengths for training a triage model. Where is this documented, and can I control the distribution?

Great question, Hannah. The count you set is a per-ticket target the generator aims to match as closely as possible, applied ticket-by-ticket rather than as a run-wide average — so you'll see close-to-exact thread lengths, with small deviations when the model can't hit the number cleanly. To vary the spread today, adjust the target and re-run; a configurable distribution is on the roadmap. I've noted the doc is thin here and we'll expand it in the prompt-compiler section.
